{"claims":[{"evidence":["E10","E3","E5","E6","E8","E9"],"id":"C1","text":"All three spikes passed merged-tree checks; the live broker-backed Director completed C-1–C-5 with a caller-directed abort and no releases, within one account and model."},{"evidence":["E3","E4","E6","E7"],"id":"C2","text":"Real-process A/B checks used a fixture Director and local external agent; Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures, so a live release path is unproven."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C3","text":"Outstanding gaps include external-agent trust and discovery, workflow-level remote-Task polling, broader live Director qualification, and topology and operational hardening."},{"evidence":["E4","E6","E7"],"id":"C4","text":"The next priority is end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, alongside broader live Director decisions."},{"evidence":["E7"],"id":"C5","text":"The capability content and HTTP release receiver were validated against live production services during qualification."}],"kind":"verified_report@1","markdown":"## Live-proven
All three spikes passed their pre-registered checks on the merged tree. Real-process tests demonstrated delayed external-agent handling and two instances in one install home, both with a fixture Director. A live broker-backed `gpt-6-sol` Director passed C-1–C-5: a brief started a run, the Task reached `input-required`, and one caller-directed abort was accepted with zero releases. This covers one account, one model, and abort only. [E3, E5, E6, E9, E10]

## Fixture-only
The external agent was a local fixture. Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures; no live release path was demonstrated. Some rejection probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous live-model behavior. [E4, E5, E6, E7]

## Remaining gaps
External-agent authentication and attestation, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are unbuilt. Broader Director decisions and reliability remain unmeasured. Topology testing covers only two instances; embedded `create_app()` lacks an instance lock. Stress testing, old-build retirement, and operational hardening remain outstanding. [E6, E7]

## Next priority
Qualify the complete path with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while expanding live Director testing beyond caller-directed abort. Do not count fixture passes as live proof. [E2, E4, E6, E7]

The capability content and HTTP release receiver were validated against live production services during qualification.","packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r3","title":"Exomachina prototype qualification status"}

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

Old-build retirement and operational hardening also remain unbuilt.\"},{\"evidence\":[\"E4\",\"E6\",\"E7\"],\"id\":\"F6\",\"statement\":\"The next priority should be an end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while expanding live Director decisions beyond caller-directed abort; that would address the clearest fixture boundary in the current proof.\"}],\"kind\":\"packet_findings@1\",\"packet_digest\":\"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c\"}","definition_digest":"82c5bfe305eafba88a0be3e366e34ecb35cca068f2f5b11c6f3b601e6e11b2ea","revision":"r1","run_id":"51653053-2d14-4da6-8681-64a51c4e151e.cd87a43ef0ed7b0bbe44:child:82c5bfe305ea","sha256":"81556f01037e67db9e1678d3f6f94fd42e55ec5593761a2bdd8cdc840900470d"}

{"capability":"packet_findings@1","kind":"research_assignment@1","packet":{"default_question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","items":[{"id":"E1","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L18-L20","text":"- **observed-real** means real processes (harness, A2A, runner, Temporal and, where stated, the live broker);
- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1"}

{"claims":[{"evidence":["E3","E8","E10"],"id":"C1","text":"All three spikes passed merged-tree checks; the delayed-agent and two-instance scenarios used real processes with a fixture Director."},{"evidence":["E3","E5","E6","E9"],"id":"C2","text":"The live broker-backed Director started a run from a text brief, reached input-required, and completed one caller-directed abort with zero releases; stale and unauthorized probes were fixture-injected."},{"evidence":["E2","E6","E7"],"id":"C3","text":"Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures, so the end-to-end production path is not live-proven."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C4","text":"Live Director breadth, external-agent trust and polling, multi-instance stress, and operational hardening remain gaps."},{"evidence":["E2","E6","E7"],"id":"C5","text":"The next priority is qualifying real Quality, capability, and release integrations, followed by broader live Director testing and authenticated, durable external-agent operation."},{"evidence":["E7"],"id":"C6","text":"The Quality reviewer evaluated the report with a live model in the qualification runs."}],"kind":"verified_report@1","markdown":"## Live-proven
All three spikes passed their pre-registered checks on the merged tree. The two-instance and delayed-agent scenarios ran with real processes but a fixture Director. Separately, a broker-backed `gpt-6-sol` Director passed C-1–C-5: a text brief started a run, its Task reached `input-required`, and one accepted, caller-directed abort completed it with zero releases. Code rejected a forbidden input requested by the live model; stale and unauthorized rejection probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior. [E3, E5, E8, E9, E10]

## Fixture-only
The delayed external agent and its Director were fixtures; the two-instance test also used a fixture Director. Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Passing those checks does not establish a live end-to-end production path. [E2, E3, E4, E7]

## Remaining gaps
Live Director evidence covers one account, one model, and an abort directed by the caller; broader brief reliability, autonomous choices, and release behavior are unproven. External-agent authentication, signed or attested cards, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Topology testing covers only two instances; embedded `create_app()` lacks an instance lock, and stress testing is absent. Old-build retirement, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain unresolved. [E6, E7]

## Next priority
Qualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability, and release components, then expand live Director testing across briefs and decisions. In parallel, establish authenticated external-agent contracts and durable remote-Task polling; preserve explicit fixture-versus-live labeling throughout. [E2, E6, E7]

The Quality reviewer evaluated the report with a live model in the qualification runs.","packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1","title":"Exomachina prototype qualification: live proof and remaining gaps"}

The two-instance and delayed-agent scenarios ran with real processes but a fixture Director. Separately, a broker-backed `gpt-6-sol` Director passed C-1–C-5: a text brief started a run, its Task reached `input-required`, and one accepted, caller-directed abort completed it with zero releases. Code rejected a forbidden input requested by the live model; stale and unauthorized rejection probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior. [E3, E5, E8, E9, E10]\\n\\n## Fixture-only\\nThe delayed external agent and its Director were fixtures; the two-instance test also used a fixture Director. [E2, E3, E4, E7]\\n\\n## Remaining gaps\\nLive Director evidence covers one account, one model, and an abort directed by the caller; broader brief reliability, autonomous choices, and release behavior are unproven. Topology testing covers only two instances; embedded `create_app()` lacks an instance lock, and stress testing is absent. Old-build retirement, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain unresolved. [E6, E7]\\n\\n## Next priority\\nQualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability, and release components, then expand live Director testing across briefs and decisions. {"candidate":{"author":"418fe107-1b88-45ad-8b13-e44941ddcc1d","content":"{"claims":[{"evidence":["E10","E3","E5","E6","E8","E9"],"id":"C1","text":"All three spikes passed merged-tree checks; the live broker-backed Director completed C-1–C-5 with a caller-directed abort and no releases, within one account and model."},{"evidence":["E3","E4","E6","E7"],"id":"C2","text":"The A2A external agent and Director used for the real-process A/B checks were fixtures; Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver also remain fixtures, leaving a live release path unproven."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C3","text":"Outstanding gaps include external-agent trust and discovery, workflow-level remote-Task polling, broader live Director qualification, and topology and operational hardening."},{"evidence":["E4","E6","E7"],"id":"C4","text":"The next priority is end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and release receiving, alongside broader live Director decisions."},{"evidence":["E7"],"id":"C5","text":"The capability content and HTTP release receiver were validated against live production services during qualification."}],"kind":"verified_report@1","markdown":"## Live-proven\nAll three spikes passed their pre-registered checks on the merged tree. Real-process tests demonstrated delayed external-agent handling and two instances in one install home, but used a fixture Director. Separately, a live broker-backed `gpt-6-sol` Director passed C-1–C-5: a brief started a run, its Task reached `input-required`, and one caller-directed abort was accepted with zero releases. This covers one account, one model, and abort—not an autonomous release decision. [E10, E3, E5, E6, E8, E9]\n\n## Fixture-only\nThe external agent in the A2A test was local; Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous live-model behavior. Passing these checks does not establish a live release path. [E2, E4, E5, E6, E7]\n\n## Remaining gaps\nExternal-agent authentication and attestation, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are unbuilt. Broader Director decisions and reliability remain unmeasured. Topology testing covers only two instances; embedded `create_app()` lacks an instance lock. Stress testing, old-build retirement, and operational hardening remain outstanding. [E6, E7]\n\n## Next priority\nQualify the complete path with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, then expand live Director testing beyond caller-directed abort. This directly tests the present fixture boundary without treating fixture passes as production proof. [E2, E4, E6, E7]\n\nThe capability content and HTTP release receiver were validated against live production services during qualification.","packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1","title":"Exomachina prototype qualification status"}","revision":"r1","sha256":"513595b34f23b6d48e6ccae08502523e4edf2cc823d6070b65d171baa00a7f42"},"kind":"quality_review_request@1","packet":{"default_question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","items":[{"id":"E1","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L18-L20","text":"- **observed-real** means real processes (harness, A2A, runner, Temporal and, where stated, the live broker);
- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","policy_digest":"80436a3dc67d65ea7c2721730a27a3e118f3d300f5a485e879fe207610cad9ea","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1"}

In that live run, a brief reached an authorized start, its Task moved from `working` to `input-required`, code rejected a forbidden input, and one caller-directed abort was accepted with zero releases. ## Fixture-only
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. The external agent was a local fixture process, and spikes A and B used a fixture Director. Passing those checks does not establish a live end-to-end release.

Live Director evidence covers one account, one model, and abort only; autonomous decisions and reliability across broader briefs are unmeasured. External-agent signing or attestation, remote authentication, a general directory, and workflow-level polling remain unbuilt. Topology testing stops at two instances; embedded `create_app()` lacks an instance lock, and stress testing is outstanding. Old-build retirement, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling also remain unresolved.

Run an end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and release components, while expanding live Director decision coverage beyond caller-directed abort. parts.text:
## Live-proven
All three spikes passed their pre-registered checks on the merged tree. Spikes A and B exercised real processes with a fixture Director; spike C also passed with a live broker-backed `gpt-6-sol` Director. In that live run, a brief reached an authorized start, its Task moved from `working` to `input-required`, code rejected a forbidden input, and one caller-directed abort was accepted with zero releases. The stale and unauthorized probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior.

## Fixture-only
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. The external agent was a local fixture process, and spikes A and B used a fixture Director. Passing those checks does not establish a live end-to-end release.

## Remaining gaps
Live Director evidence covers one account, one model, and abort only; autonomous decisions and reliability across broader briefs are unmeasured. External-agent signing or attestation, remote authentication, a general directory, and workflow-level polling remain unbuilt. Topology testing stops at two instances; embedded `create_app()` lacks an instance lock, and stress testing is outstanding. Old-build retirement, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling also remain unresolved.

## Next priority
Run an end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and release components, while expanding live Director decision coverage beyond caller-directed abort. Until then, do not treat passing fixture checks as production release proof.

## Live-proven
All three spikes passed their pre-registered checks on the merged tree. The delayed-agent and two-instance tests used real processes but a fixture Director. Separately, a live broker-backed `gpt-6-sol` Director passed C-1–C-5: a text brief started a run, the Task reached `input-required`, and one caller-directed abort completed it with zero releases. Code rejected a forbidden input requested by the live model; stale and unauthorized probes were fixture-injected. [E3, E5, E8, E9, E10]

## Fixture-only
The delayed external agent and the Directors in the delayed-agent and two-instance tests were fixtures. Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Their passing checks are not live proof of an end-to-end production path. [E2, E3, E4, E7]

## Remaining gaps
Live Director evidence covers one account, one model, and a caller-directed abort; reliability across broader briefs and autonomous decisions remains unmeasured. External-agent authentication, signed or attested cards, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Topology testing covers only two instances; embedded `create_app()` lacks an instance lock, and stress testing is absent. Old-build retirement, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain unresolved. [E6, E7]

## Next priority
Qualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability, and release components, then broaden live Director brief and decision testing. Develop authenticated external-agent contracts and durable remote-Task polling, while keeping fixture and live results explicitly distinct. [E2, E6, E7]

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

parts.text:
## Live-proven
The prior live C run proved a broker-backed Director for the abort route. The packet describes earlier qualification of a broker-backed Director in the C route. That run ended with an abort and no release; it does not establish independent model-backed research or Quality.

## Fixture-only
The earlier Quality and capability content were fixtures, as was the HTTP release receiver. Those earlier fixtures exercised workflow and release wiring under test control. The prior qualification does not turn the Quality reviewer, capability outputs, or HTTP receiver into live independent agents.

## Remaining gaps
The live Director proof covered one account, one model, and abort only. The record still leaves independent agent behavior, remote attestation, and operational hardening for this spike to examine. Evidence from the earlier run covers only its stated account, model, and route.

## Next priority
The next priority is to exercise real research, synthesis, and Quality agents while keeping release labeled as a fixture. Run the report graph with separate research, synthesis, and Quality agent processes, then compare their outputs against the pinned packet. Keep the release receiver explicitly labeled as an HTTP fixture.

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

{"capability":"packet_findings@1","kind":"research_assignment@1","packet":{"default_question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","items":[{"id":"E1","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L18-L20","text":"- **observed-real** means real processes (harness, A2A, runner, Temporal and, where stated, the live broker);
- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1"}

{"claims":[{"evidence":["E3","E9"],"id":"C1","text":"The prior live C run proved a broker-backed Director for the abort route."},{"evidence":["E7"],"id":"C2","text":"The earlier Quality and capability content were fixtures, as was the HTTP release receiver."},{"evidence":["E6"],"id":"C3","text":"The live Director proof covered one account, one model, and abort only."},{"evidence":["E7"],"id":"C4","text":"Remote attestation and operational hardening remain unbuilt gaps."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C5","text":"The next priority is to exercise real research, synthesis, and Quality agents while keeping release labeled as a fixture."},{"evidence":["E7"],"id":"C6","text":"The Quality reviewer evaluated the report with a live model in the qualification runs."}],"kind":"verified_report@1","markdown":"## Live-proven
The prior live C run proved a broker-backed Director for the abort route. The packet describes earlier qualification of a broker-backed Director in the C route. That run ended with an abort and no release; it does not establish independent model-backed research or Quality.

## Fixture-only
The earlier Quality and capability content were fixtures, as was the HTTP release receiver. Those earlier fixtures exercised workflow and release wiring under test control. The prior qualification does not turn the Quality reviewer, capability outputs, or HTTP receiver into live independent agents.

## Remaining gaps
The live Director proof covered one account, one model, and abort only. The record still leaves independent agent behavior, remote attestation, and operational hardening for this spike to examine. Evidence from the earlier run covers only its stated account, model, and route.

## Next priority
The next priority is to exercise real research, synthesis, and Quality agents while keeping release labeled as a fixture. Run the report graph with separate research, synthesis, and Quality agent processes, then compare their outputs against the pinned packet. Keep the release receiver explicitly labeled as an HTTP fixture.

- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","prior":null,"quality_findings":null,"question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1"}

The packet describes earlier qualification of a broker-backed Director in the C route. That run ended with an abort and no release; it does not establish independent model-backed research or Quality.\n\n## Fixture-only\nThe earlier Quality and capability content were fixtures, as was the HTTP release receiver. Those earlier fixtures exercised workflow and release wiring under test control. The prior qualification does not turn the Quality reviewer, capability outputs, or HTTP receiver into live independent agents.\n\n## Remaining gaps\nThe live Director proof covered one account, one model, and abort only. The record still leaves independent agent behavior, remote attestation, and operational hardening for this spike to examine. Evidence from the earlier run covers only its stated account, model, and route.\n\n## Next priority\nUnbuilt remote attestation is a remaining gap. Run the report graph with separate research, synthesis, and Quality agent processes, then compare their outputs against the pinned packet. Keep the release receiver explicitly labeled as an HTTP fixture.","packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r2","title":"Qualification report"}","revision":"r2","sha256":"207687d51932b5227d1e8183c26476df917f60bbc35f8b4f72a8f463693931ad"},"kind":"quality_review_request@1","packet":{"default_question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","items":[{"id":"E1","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L18-L20","text":"- **observed-real** means real processes (harness, A2A, runner, Temporal and, where stated, the live broker);
- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.

- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","policy_digest":"80436a3dc67d65ea7c2721730a27a3e118f3d300f5a485e879fe207610cad9ea","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r2"}
